---
title: "Building a Windows DFIR box"
subtitle: "Build a repeatable Windows workstation for analyzing evidence that has already been collected."
---

## What we're building

- A Windows analysis machine, not an evidence acquisition machine.
- Evidence is already collected; memory acquisition is handled separately (Magnet in our workflow).

The box takes collected artifacts (triage collections, event logs, registry hives, disk images, memory images) and produces analysis output: parsed CSVs, timelines, notes. It never touches the client's systems.

This is an opinionated build. Each choice below has alternatives; these are the ones that have worked.

| | Choice | Why |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Windows | Windows Server 2025, Desktop Experience | Stable Long-Term Servicing Channel release; Microsoft Defender Antivirus is a feature you can remove; no TPM requirement |
| Hypervisor | VMware Workstation Pro | Independent non-persistent disks reset on power-off; Shared Folders, one of them read-only, keep case data outside the VM |
| Install | An unattend file | The same Windows build every time, with the settings below already applied |
| Settings | UAC off, Defender removed, long paths on, extensions and hidden files shown | Analysis tools run without friction on a machine that is thrown away |
| Tools | Chocolatey, plus a few direct downloads | One command line installs most of the list, and records versions |

## Disposable/nonpersistent virtual machine

- Return the machine to a known state.
- Keep case data and analysis output separate from what gets reset.

**Why disposable.** Analysis tools open hostile files. Each case starts from the same known-good image, nothing carries over from the previous client, and "what version of the tool did we use" has one answer.

### VMware Workstation Pro

Workstation Pro has been free for commercial, educational and personal use since November 2024 ([Broadcom](https://knowledge.broadcom.com/external/article/368667/download-and-license-vmware-desktop-hypervisor.html)); download it from the Broadcom support portal.

| | Lives where | On reset |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Windows, settings, installed tools | System disk, **independent non-persistent** | Discarded at power-off |
| Temporary files, caches, tool state | System disk | Discarded at power-off |
| Evidence | Host folder, shared **read-only** | Kept; the VM cannot change it |
| Analysis output, tool logs, notes | Host folder, shared read-write | Kept |

**Non-persistent system disk.** Build the VM with a normal disk, install and configure everything, shut it down, then in **VM Settings → Hard Disk → Advanced** set the disk to *Independent* and *Nonpersistent*. From then on, changes are discarded when you power off the VM or restore a snapshot, and the disk is in the same state every time it starts ([VMware Workstation Pro documentation](https://docs.vmware.com/en/VMware-Workstation-Pro/17/com.vmware.ws.using.doc/GUID-A6792F54-2734-4AF4-9473-C8B9AD8321AF.html)). A restart inside Windows is not a power-off; shut down, and power the VM off. To update the image, switch the disk back to persistent, update, and switch it back.

**Shared Folders.** In **VM Settings → Options → Shared Folders**, add two host folders: `Evidence` with the **Read-only** attribute, so the VM can view and copy files but cannot add, change or remove them, and `Cases` read-write for output. With VMware Tools installed, they appear in Windows at `\\vmware-host\Shared Folders\`. Host file permissions still apply.

**Verify it.** Write a test file to `Cases`, try (and fail) to write one to `Evidence`, power off, power on, and confirm the `Cases` file is still there and a file you left on the desktop is gone.

## Automating the build

- Decide on the Windows image and tool list.
- Make setup repeatable rather than configuring it by hand each time.

### Windows Server 2025

Use the Desktop Experience installation option; the analysis tools need a desktop. Microsoft's [Evaluation Center](https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/evalcenter/download-windows-server-2025) has a 180-day evaluation, which must be activated online within its first 10 days or it shuts down; activate it during the build, while the VM has a network. A licensed image is the alternative. Why Server rather than Windows 11:

- **Stable.** Long-Term Servicing Channel: no feature updates rearranging the system between cases.
- **Defender is a feature.** On Windows Server, Microsoft Defender Antivirus is installed as a Windows feature, `Windows-Defender`, so it can be removed cleanly instead of fought with ([Microsoft Learn](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/defender-endpoint/microsoft-defender-antivirus-windows-server-configure)).
- **No TPM requirement.** Microsoft lists a TPM as "required only for certain features," such as BitLocker ([hardware requirements](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows-server/get-started/hardware-requirements)), so the VM needs no virtual TPM, and no encryption of the VM that a virtual TPM brings with it in Workstation.

### Unattended install

An unattend file (`autounattend.xml`) answers every question Windows Setup asks and can apply settings and run scripts. Build one with [Christoph Schneegans' unattend generator](https://schneegans.de/windows/unattend-generator/). Settings to choose for this box:

| Generator setting | Why |
| --- | --- |
| A local administrator account | No Microsoft account; one known login |
| Disable User Account Control (UAC) | See [UAC](#uac) below |
| Enable long paths | Deep paths inside collections otherwise fail |
| Always show file extensions; show all files | `invoice.pdf.exe` and hidden files are visible |
| Do not update Last Access Time stamp | Reading a file on the box does not change its last access time |
| Disable SmartScreen | Tools downloaded during the build are not blocked |
| Remove bloatware | Fewer distractions and background updates |
| FirstLogon scripts | Install Chocolatey and the tools ([below](#tools-for-analysis)) |

The generator is written for Windows 10 and 11. Most of these settings are ordinary setup and registry settings that apply to Windows Server 2025 too, but test the file on Server before relying on it. Generate it again when you change the build, rather than editing the XML by hand.

Windows Setup looks for `autounattend.xml` in the root of removable media. In Workstation, create the VM with **I will install the operating system later** (so VMware's Easy Install does not supply its own answers), attach the Windows ISO, and attach a second small ISO, or a floppy image, containing `autounattend.xml`.

## Configuring Windows for analysis

- Tools that need to run as administrator.
- UAC: normally I don't disable security features, but this is a disposable VM and reducing friction matters.
- Other Windows security settings as decisions specific to this machine, not general recommendations.

These are the settings, and the command for each if you apply it after setup instead of in the unattend file. Run them in an elevated PowerShell.

| Setting | Command |
| --- | --- |
| UAC off | `Set-ItemProperty -Path HKLM:\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Policies\System -Name EnableLUA -Value 0`, then restart |
| Remove Microsoft Defender Antivirus | `Uninstall-WindowsFeature -Name Windows-Defender`, then restart (check the name with `Get-WindowsFeature *defender*`) |
| Long paths | `Set-ItemProperty -Path HKLM:\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Control\FileSystem -Name LongPathsEnabled -Value 1` |
| Show file extensions | `Set-ItemProperty -Path HKCU:\Software\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Explorer\Advanced -Name HideFileExt -Value 0` |
| Show hidden files | Same key: `Hidden` = 1 |
| Show protected system files | Same key: `ShowSuperHidden` = 1 |
| No last-access updates | `fsutil behavior set disablelastaccess 1` |
| Server Manager not at every logon | `Get-ScheduledTask -TaskName ServerManager \| Disable-ScheduledTask` |

### UAC {#uac}

With `EnableLUA` = 0, Admin Approval Mode is off and administrators run everything elevated, so tools that need administrator rights simply work. The middle ground is `ConsentPromptBehaviorAdmin` = 0: UAC stays on and elevates without prompting, but programs still start unelevated unless asked. See Microsoft's [User Account Control settings and configuration](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/security/application-security/application-control/user-account-control/settings-and-configuration).

### Network and updates

Analysis rarely needs the internet; installs and tool updates do. Connect the VM during the build, then use a host-only network (or none) during cases. Windows Update in the middle of a case changes the system under the analysis; update the clean image on a schedule instead.

## Tools for analysis

- Select the tools and versions.
- KAPE modules for processing already-collected artifacts.

### Chocolatey and Scoop

[Chocolatey](https://chocolatey.org/install) installs most of the list from one command, which makes the FirstLogon step one line. Its community packages are maintained by volunteers, separately from the tools' authors: check the package page links to the real project before adding it. [Scoop](https://scoop.sh/) is an alternative that installs per user without administrator rights; it has fewer DFIR tools.

```powershell
choco install -y 7zip sysinternals pwsh ericzimmermantools volatility3 autopsy
```

Record what is installed for the case notes, and pin versions (`--version`) once the list settles so every rebuild is the same:

```powershell
choco list | Out-File -FilePath "\\vmware-host\Shared Folders\Cases\2026-0142\Notes\Tools.txt"
```

### The tool list

| Tool | For | Install |
| --- | --- | --- |
| [Eric Zimmerman's tools](https://ericzimmerman.github.io/) | Registry, event logs, MFT, LNK, jump lists; Timeline Explorer for the CSVs | `choco install ericzimmermantools`, or his `Get-ZimmermanTools.ps1` |
| [KAPE](https://www.kroll.com/kape) | Running modules over a collection | Download from Kroll after registering; see licensing below |
| [FTK Imager](https://www.exterro.com/digital-forensics-software/ftk-imager) | Mounting and browsing disk images | Download from Exterro |
| [Volatility 3](https://github.com/volatilityfoundation/volatility3) | Memory images | `choco install volatility3` |
| [log2timeline / plaso](https://plaso.readthedocs.io/) | Super timelines | Docker on Windows ([plaso documentation](https://plaso.readthedocs.io/en/latest/sources/user/Users-Guide.html)); inside this VM that needs nested virtualization, so a separate Linux VM is often simpler |
| [Chainsaw](https://github.com/WithSecureLabs/chainsaw) | Hunting through event logs with Sigma rules | Release zip from GitHub (Chocolatey's `chainsaw` is a different program) |
| [Hayabusa](https://github.com/Yamato-Security/hayabusa) | Event log timelines and Sigma detections | Release zip from GitHub |
| [Autopsy](https://www.sleuthkit.org/autopsy/) | Disk image analysis | `choco install autopsy` |
| Microsoft Office | Documents, and Excel for the CSVs | If your license covers it |
| 7-Zip, Sysinternals, PowerShell 7 | The basics | In the `choco` line above |

Record the version of every tool used for a case in the case notes.

### Processing an existing artifact set with KAPE modules

KAPE has two halves: **targets** collect files from a system, and **modules** run programs against files already collected. For this box only modules apply. Modules are defined in `.mkape` files; the community set is maintained in [KapeFiles](https://github.com/EricZimmerman/KapeFiles), which includes the compound module `!EZParser` (runs Eric Zimmerman's parsers over a collection).

```powershell
# Module source is a collection that already exists; output goes to case storage.
.\kape.exe --msource "\\vmware-host\Shared Folders\Evidence\2026-0142\C" --mdest "\\vmware-host\Shared Folders\Cases\2026-0142\Output\EZParser" --module !EZParser
```

Check the switches against `kape.exe --help` and the [KAPE documentation](https://ericzimmerman.github.io/KapeDocs/) for the version you install.

**Licensing.** Kroll's KAPE terms distinguish free use from uses that require an enterprise license, including use on third-party networks or as part of a paid engagement. Check which applies to your work: [KAPE license agreement](https://www.kroll.com/en/kape-license-agreement).

## Using and resetting the box

- Run tools against existing artifacts.
- Retain the results and relevant logs.
- Verify the environment and reset it for the next case.

A per-case checklist:

1. Power on from the non-persistent image. Confirm `\\vmware-host\Shared Folders\Evidence` is read-only and `Cases` is writable.
2. Create the case folders with `New-CaseFolder` from the [CrtEssentials module](powershell.qmd#module), and put the evidence in the host's `Evidence` folder. Hash it on arrival with `Get-FileInventory`.
3. Run tools against `Evidence`, writing to `Cases\<case>\Output`. Keep each tool's console log or log file in `Output`.
4. Before power-off, confirm the output is on the `Cases` share: `Get-FileInventory -Path <case>\Output | Export-Csv <case>\Notes\OutputInventory.csv -NoTypeInformation`.
5. Power off. Everything on the system disk is discarded; the next case starts clean.
